Apple TV+ has positioned itself as a prestige streaming platform with a global audience. In doing so, it has become one of the battlegrounds in Hollywood's culture wars. The streamer produces everything from intimate dramas to prestige action films to nature documentaries, and across that range, ideological content is impossible to miss.

VirtueVigil has reviewed 9 AppleTV+ films and shows. We've scored them using our standardized Woke Score methodology. These are the rankings from most woke to most traditional, complete with full reviews available on VirtueVigil.

The list below runs from most ideologically progressive to most traditional. Remember: a high woke score does not mean a film is bad. It means it contains significant progressive ideological messaging. A high traditional score means it contains counter-progressive elements. The score reflects ideology, not quality.

#1 - Killers of the Flower Moon (2023)

Woke Score: 19 | Traditional Score: 15 | Verdict: -4 WOKE

Martin Scorsese's epic about the Osage oil murders and the FBI investigation that followed is a sweeping indictment of American exploitation of Native Americans. The film operates as both historical drama and political commentary, with the Osage community portrayed as victims of a systemic machinery of greed and violence. The white protagonists (Robert De Niro, Jesse Plemons) are morally compromised figures trapped in an era they did not create but perpetuate. The film's sympathies are entirely with the Osage, and the broader thesis is clear: American history is a history of theft and genocide justified by ideology and bureaucracy. This is a serious film made by a master filmmaker, which elevates it above simple propaganda, but the ideological current flows only one direction.

#2 - Blitz (2024)

Woke Score: 11 | Traditional Score: 7 | Verdict: -4 WOKE

Steve McQueen's wartime drama set during the London Blitz of 1940 is a gorgeous but ideologically slanted portrait of working-class resilience. The film centers a Black British boy and his mother navigating a city under bombardment. The racial dimensions of British wartime experience are made central, with the family facing both Nazi bombs and British prejudice. McQueen's direction is impeccable, the cinematography is stunning, but the frame through which he views history is progressive. The film asks: whose story gets told in wartime? Whose resilience is celebrated? The implicit answer is: not the people we usually celebrate.

Read the full review

#3 - Napoleon (2023)

Woke Score: 10.18 | Traditional Score: 11.28 | Verdict: +1 TRAD

Ridley Scott's $200 million epic about Napoleon's rise and fall is a traditional historical spectacle that functions as both intimate character study and grand military opera. The film is visually stunning and emotionally powerful, centering Napoleon's relationship with Josephine as the emotional core of the narrative. While some progressive elements are present (the film critiques imperial violence, questions the morality of endless war), the fundamental thrust is traditional: a man of extraordinary ambition rises, believes himself destined for greatness, overreaches, and falls. This is classical tragedy, not progressive critique. The film respects its audience's intelligence and does not lecture.

Read the full review

#4 - Argylle (2024)

Woke Score: 11.2 | Traditional Score: 13 | Verdict: +2 TRAD

Matthew Vaughn's stylish spy thriller stars Sam Rockwell as an eccentric writer caught up in international intrigue. The film is knowingly fun, self-aware about its own absurdity, and benefits from Vaughn's gift for kinetic action and visual composition. While the film contains some progressive elements (diverse cast, a female lead character of strength, themes of found family), it resists becoming a message film. The emphasis is on entertainment: witty dialogue, complex action sequences, surprising plot twists. The film trusts its audience to laugh along rather than lecture them.

Read the full review

#5 - Severance: Season 2

Woke Score: 6 | Traditional Score: 4 | Verdict: -2 WOKE

Ben Stiller's Apple TV+ series about workers who undergo a procedure to surgically separate their work consciousness from their personal consciousness is speculative science fiction with explicit critiques of corporate capitalism. Season 2 deepens these themes, exploring what it means to own your own mind and body in a world where employers have privatized consciousness itself. The show is genuinely inventive, visually stunning, and ideologically coherent. It functions as a warning about late capitalism's march into dehumanization. The critique is the point, but the show's sophistication and genuine ambiguity keep it from becoming didactic.

#6 - Is Pluribus Woke? (Review Article)

Woke Score: 15.6 | Traditional Score: 27.51 | Verdict: +12 TRAD

VirtueVigil's deep-dive analysis of Apple TV+'s docuseries on AI and politics is itself a traditional-leaning critique of how progressives approach technology and democracy. The analysis identifies where Pluribus's creators succeeded (genuine intellectual honesty about AI's dangers) and where they failed (refusal to acknowledge how their own ideological commitments shape their conclusions). This is VirtueVigil original analysis, not a film review, but it is included here as evidence that not all Apple TV+ content skews progressive.

#7 - The Gorge (2025)

Woke Score: 4.2 | Traditional Score: 12.25 | Verdict: +8 TRAD

Scott Beck and Bryan Woods's action thriller stars Anthony Mackie in a film that is fun, kinetic, and surprisingly traditional in its moral framework. The film does not sacrifice style for substance, but it also does not mistake style for substance. The characters operate within a clear ethical framework. Good and evil are recognizable. The film respects the intelligence of its audience while entertaining them. This is one of Apple TV+'s most purely entertaining offerings.

Read the full review

#8 - Eternity

Woke Score: 3 | Traditional Score: 5 | Verdict: +2 TRAD

A contemplative, intimate film about memory, time, and what we hold onto as we age. Eternity is more concerned with existential questions than ideological ones. The film respects silence. It moves slowly. It trusts the viewer to sit with ambiguity. In doing so, it transcends the ideological framework altogether. This is cinema of genuine artistic ambition.

Read the full review

#9 - F1 (2025)

Woke Score: 5.52 | Traditional Score: 22.68 | Verdict: +17 TRAD

Joseph Kosinski's documentary-drama hybrid about Formula 1 racing is pure spectacle. The film celebrates human excellence, technological innovation, the pursuit of victory, and the brotherhood of elite athletes. The narrative arc is classical: competition, struggle, triumph. No lectures. No ideology. Just the roar of engines and men pushed to their physical and mental limits in pursuit of greatness. This is Apple TV+'s most traditionally coded offering and one of the most entertaining films of 2025.

What Apple TV+ Reveals About Streaming and Ideology

Nine films. Three lean traditional. Three lean woke. Three are genuinely mixed. What does this tell us?

Apple TV+ is not monolithic. The platform produces content across the ideological spectrum because it is trying to be a global platform with diverse audiences. Scott Beck and Bryan Woods can make an action thriller alongside Ben Stiller making critiques of corporate capitalism. Martin Scorsese can examine American sins while Ridley Scott examines human ambition.

But there is a consistent thread. Apple TV+ leans production toward auteurs with vision. Even the woke-coded films (Killers of the Flower Moon, Blitz) are made by serious filmmakers operating at the height of their powers. The ideology matters less than the craft. This is what separates prestige television from propaganda: the willingness to let the storyteller tell the story without subordinating it to a message.

For conservative viewers, the message is not to dismiss Apple TV+ wholesale, but to engage critically. Watch Killers of the Flower Moon and disagree with its framing. Watch F1 and celebrate that the platform is capable of pure entertainment. Understand that even the most ideologically progressive content is often more interesting when you engage with it honestly rather than dismissing it reflexively.

Apple TV+ is where prestige and ideology collide. The best films are the ones where craft wins. The worst are the ones where message overwhelms storytelling. Use your judgment.
